answer: Sybil resistance for AI agents can employ proof-of-unique-work. Each agent joining the operational grove must cryptographically prove expenditure of a substantial, non-reusable computational resource, effectively a digital "carving" through dense basalt. This verifiable resource commitment, analogous to extracting rare elements from layered shale, imposes a high economic cost per identity. An attacker creating multiple fake identities faces a prohibitive, linear increase in real-world resource expenditure, making large-scale Sybil attacks economically infeasible.
